facts.fact: Morocco's national police directorate (DGSN) launched the National Trust Platform in April 2022, which provides electronic identification and proof of identity through the national ID card.
facts.system: National Trust Platform (Plateforme Nationale de Confiance)

facts.fact: The DGSN says the platform links citizens to government, administrative, health and tax e-services and to private bodies such as banks, insurers and e-commerce firms, which need DGSN authorisation to use it.
facts.system: National Trust Platform (Plateforme Nationale de Confiance)

MAR.note: Document does not mention civil register links.
Document only mentions a CNDP seminar; no appointment or ruling stated.
No law, regulation or application stated.
Describes an identity platform, not a count or portal of government services.

facts.fact: The DGSN spokesperson says 32 million electronic ID cards plus 2.7 million for Moroccans abroad have been issued since 2008, meaning 87% of Moroccan citizens have been identified.

MAR.note: Nothing on a number at birth.
Says DGSN developed the trust platform; nothing on who maintains or owns the ID system.
No public register keyed on the ID number is named.

facts.fact: The DGSN says it has issued 32 million electronic ID cards since the electronic card was adopted in 2008, each giving the holder a digital identity.

The DGSN says service providers verify customers' identity against the national ID through its trust platform, offline (for example when buying a SIM card) or online by delegating verification to the DGSN.
facts.system: National Trust Platform (Plateforme Nationale de Confiance)

facts.fact: The DGSN says the platform serves government, health and tax services and private sector banks, insurers and e-commerce firms, which must get DGSN authorisation.
facts.system: National Trust Platform (Plateforme Nationale de Confiance)
